programs.title: Agents Work, Members Govern: A Worker Introduction to Agent-Managed DAOs
outcomes: Explain how 'Agents operate; people govern' protects worker voice in automated systems
Read a DAO charter and identify the five human-reserved actions
Draft a member proposal for the Proposal Forum
Evaluate agent-generated evidence summaries for workplace decisions

sessions.activity: Guided reading of the Series 17 charter, mission and contribution model; small groups map which powers stay with people and which go to agents, using the Blue Lagoon setting as a case of shared natural resources.
Learners review sample Evidence Monitor outputs, practice checking claims against sources, and flag missing evidence in a structured worksheet.
Each group drafts a short member proposal (problem, action, measurable outcome) for agent pre-drafting, then debates another group's draft in a mock human final vote.
Role-play task routing: learners assign tasks to agents and working groups, observing that agents never enact treasury transfers or appointments.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized proposal-draft quality rubric scores and common questions about governance roles, aggregated to improve the Proposal & Grant Drafter's templates.
programs.consent: Participation is voluntary; adult learners opt in at enrollment and may withdraw anytime. No personal identifiers are collected; only anonymized rubric scores are pooled.

programs.title: Lava Fields and Rules: Exploring Governance in a Geothermal Wonderland
outcomes: Describe the Blue Lagoon and Reykjanes lava field biome (desert, geothermal lake) and why geothermal water is warm
Explain what a DAO is in simple terms and why some decisions stay with people
Compare rules in nature (lava fields) with rules in a community charter
Create a class charter with human-reserved decisions

sessions.activity: Story-based introduction: a spa in a black lava field run by helpful robot assistants. Students learn 'robots help, people decide' and sort decision cards into agent vs. human piles.
Students act as Evidence Monitors: examine simple 'fact cards' about geothermal heat and lava fields, mark which have sources and which are guesses.
Class writes and debates one simple proposal (e.g., a recycling rule for a pretend spa), then votes together, seeing that only students cast the final vote.
Students design a progress chart with measurable outcomes for their class charter and track it over one week, like the Progress Tracker agent.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized class-level tallies of decision-card sorting and one-word reflections; no individual student responses are shared.
programs.consent: Written guardian/parent consent required for all data contributions; only aggregate class data leaves the classroom, teachers de-identify everything, and families may opt out at any time.

programs.title: Evidence to Action: NGO Training on Agent-Drafted, Human-Decided Grant Cycles
outcomes: Map an NGO program onto a charter with measurable outcomes
Use agent-generated research syntheses to strengthen a funding proposal
Run a decision cycle where agents draft and humans enact
Identify partnership opportunities via collaborator scouting methods

sessions.activity: Workshop on turning field program data into evidence briefs; learners practice summarizing evidence the way the Research Synthesis Agent would for stewards.
Teams convert an evidence brief into a grant-style proposal using the Proposal & Grant Drafter workflow, then simulate human-only final vote and enactment steps.
Learners do a collaborator-mapping exercise modeled on the Collaborator Scout: identify experts and partner organizations without inventing claims, verifying each against public sources.
Teams define 2-3 measurable outcomes for their own NGO program and build a progress-tracking dashboard template.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized proposal rubric results and outcome-indicator patterns (no program names or beneficiary data), aggregated to improve shared grant-drafting templates.
programs.consent: Staff opt in through their organizations; only de-identified rubric and indicator data is shared, with organizational approval and an easy withdrawal path.

programs.title: Stewarding Shared Resources: Nonprofit Governance Lessons from a Geothermal Commons
outcomes: Apply public-good governance principles to a nonprofit board context
Understand the human-reserved actions model as a check on automation
Draft measurable charter outcomes for a mission-driven organization
Practice steward-level review of agent-drafted materials

sessions.activity: Board-level seminar comparing nonprofit bylaws with the DAO charter: reserved powers, mission alignment, and contribution models, using the Blue Lagoon commons as a discussion case.
Stewards-in-training review a mock agent-drafted proposal, mark strengths and gaps, then conduct a recorded human final vote to experience the enactment boundary.
Leaders critique two evidence summaries for rigor and source quality, learning what to ask agents before trusting a synthesis.
Each participant drafts measurable outcomes for their own nonprofit and receives peer feedback using the Progress Tracker format.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized governance-checklist completion rates and commonly cited charter gaps, pooled to strengthen shared steward training materials.
programs.consent: Individual leaders consent at registration; shared data is fully anonymized and optional, with withdrawal honored without affecting participation.
